verdict.headline: Warsh signals inflation work unfinished; September hike odds jump to 59%
verdict.label: Chip selloff on hawkish Warsh; curve flattens while 30Y holds inside regime trigger
verdict.rationale_short: Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote — delivered after the morning brief was generated — concluded that summer PCE/CPI improvements 'do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved,' lifting September hike odds from 33% to 59% and dragging the chip complex 4–10% lower. The 30Y counterintuitively fell to 5.17% as the 2Y rose 9bps to 4.32%, a curve-flattening outcome: the bond market priced a near-term hike alongside slower long-run growth. The 5.30% regime trigger was not breached. The August jobs report on September 4 is now the deciding print; above 200K payrolls with AHE above 0.3% cements the hike and tests 5.30%.

trade_setups.thesis: September hike odds at 59% lifted the 2Y +9bps to 4.32% while the 30Y fell 3bps to 5.17% — a curve-flattening outcome consistent with pricing a near-term hike followed by eventual economic slowdown. The spread now sits around 85bps and is narrowing. The August jobs report (September 4) is the next inflection: a hot print tightens the spread further; a soft print reverses it as hike odds unwind.
trade_setups.entry: Spread at approximately 85bps (5.17% minus 4.32%). Below 75bps confirms accelerating flattening; a move back above 100bps on a jobs miss signals the hike scenario unwinding.
trade_setups.invalidation: Spread widens above 100bps on soft August jobs data (below 150K payrolls, AHE below 0.2%)

trade_setups.thesis: NVDA reversed from Thursday's $227.98 to $217.55 Friday, driven by Warsh's hawkish signal and a broad semi sector risk-off. The $215-220 zone is the structural support established by the two institutional-confirmation closes on August 26-27. A sustained close below $215 would extend the distribution toward the September gap fill at $205-210; a recovery above $225 with volume after the jobs print confirms the support held.
trade_setups.entry: The levels that define this setup: $215 as the structural floor, $225 as recovery confirmation. The AVGO earnings read-through on September 4-5 adds a second catalyst window within the same timeframe.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two consecutive closes above $225 on above-average volume confirm floor held; close below $215 extends distribution
trade_setups.horizon: September 2-9 (first post-Labor Day sessions through AVGO earnings)

trade_setups.thesis: BTC moved above $81,000 intraday Friday before the Warsh DXY bid (+0.4%) pulled it back. Thursday's $80,257 was the first confirmed close above $80K in four attempts; Friday added an intraday high but not a second confirmed close. The two-consecutive-closes criterion for resistance-to-support conversion is not yet met. Bessent Treasury buybacks starting September 9 provide structural demand; the September 2 first-session-back reaction to Warsh will be the next data point.
trade_setups.entry: Two consecutive closes above $80K confirm the level as support. The intraday $81K touch establishes the next upside reference. A close below $76,661 (August 24 intraday low) signals range-top behavior rather than a confirmed break.
trade_setups.invalidation: Close above $81,000 sustained into September 9 alongside Bessent buyback launch confirms structural break; close below $76,661 on September 2 signals range failure

bear_case: At 59% the September hike probability is the most aggressive near-term policy pricing of the cycle, and the bond market's curve-flattening response — front end up, long end down — historically precedes the steepest equity drawdowns in the 60 days following a cycle-first hike. The Bessent buyback program suppressing the 30Y is temporary structural demand, not fundamental demand: if Treasury Q4 supply overwhelms the $4B+ per-operation buyback bid, the 30Y breaks 5.30% simultaneously with peak hike-cycle pricing. The hot-jobs / Canada-tariff-cost-push two-variable scenario is what the market is not pricing at 59%; if August payrolls print above 200K with AHE above 0.3%, the FOMC hike becomes near-certain and tariff-side inflation enters September 8-16 Fed communications. If SPX falls below 7,600 on the jobs report, this session's weekly gains are erased and the rate-channel multiple compression is live.
